payload.name: Contrast Effects
payload.fact: In multiple reinforcement schedules, responding in one component is influenced by the reinforcement rate in other components.

provenance.quote_or_locus: for multiple schedules (i.e., successive discrimination procedures), there are contrast effects between responding in each component and reinforcement in the others

decision_note: Rejected as instructed. Note for the record: this one is NOT actually an fMRI/neural finding (its boundary is behavioral — reinforcement schedules) so the collective 'neural correlates' framing given for the other three does not literally describe it. Content-grounded rationale instead: it describes a comparative, multi-component reinforcement-schedule interaction (responding in one component depends on rates in OTHER components) rather than a single actionable lever, and its lever overlaps the approved dopamine-reward-prediction-error-sig without adding a distinct mechanism.
